title: Shared definitions and id conventions
$comment: The id space is the load-bearing part of the whole design: the five tiers are one dataset split by access pattern, joined only by these ids (invariant #1), and every doc claim cites them as evidence (invariant #2). Drift here is expensive because each later stage references them, so the conventions are pinned as patterns rather than left to convention.

identifier.$comment: A TypeScript identifier. Deliberately excludes '<' and '>' so template placeholders like '<name>' fail validation rather than passing as data.

unitId.$comment: <kind>:<path>:<ClassName> — three colon-separated parts. The path segment is relative to the Angular source root. Note the arity: this is what distinguishes a 'model:' unit id from a 'model:' two-way-binding member id, which has two parts.

memberId.$comment: <prefix>:<propertyName> — a symbol owned by one unit. 'model:' here is the two-way binding member (model<T>()), two parts, versus the three-part unit id above.

templateNodeId.$comment: Template nodes and host bindings. Cited as evidence by uiRequirements and by analysis.json.

synthesizedId.$comment: Numbered entities the Synthesizer emits into analysis.json and template.json#/uiRequirements. These are never cited as evidence by an ast tier -- evidence flows one way, from doc to ast.

evidenceId.$comment: What a doc claim may cite. Excludes synthesizedId: evidence must resolve to something extracted, never to another inference, or claims could support each other in a cycle with no grounding in source.

provenanceSource.$comment: 'hand-derived' covers the Phase A baseline, which is neither extractor output nor model output. Without it the baseline cannot be validated by the same schema as real output, and an unvalidatable baseline is a poor diff target for Phase 1.

callSiteId.$comment: Somewhere code can call from. Not every caller is a method: a field initializer runs during construction (before ngOnInit), and a template binding or host listener calls in from outside the class entirely. The POC reached for 'field-initializer:<name>' and had no id for it -- see plans/3_PhaseAFindings.md F5a.
